title.en: Practice Sheet: Python Tools for ML

summary.en: Practise array shapes, broadcasting, pandas selection and honest plotting with paper and Python.
summary.bn: কাগজে আর Python-এ array shape, broadcasting, pandas selection ও সঠিক ছবি আঁকার অনুশীলন করো।

notes: Python syntax works on 3.10+; Python 3.12 is recommended.
Use NumPy 2.0+, pandas 2.2+, scikit-learn 1.5+ and Matplotlib 3.8+ on a compatible Python.

sections.title: Mark the reason as well as the result

practice.title: Build the feature table
practice.statementHtml: Read exactly ten integers as five consecutive (size, sweetness) pairs. Print the matrix shape, then the two column sums as a Python list. Preserve the given pairings.
hints: Reshape once to (5,2), then reduce along axis zero.

practice.title: Group the real course cards
practice.statementHtml: Read size_cm or sweetness. Load tiny_fruits.csv and group by label. Print one line per group in alphabetical label order as label:count:mean, with the mean to one decimal place.
hints: Select the requested numeric column after groupby, then aggregate count and mean.

practice.title: Preserve aligned features and labels
practice.statementHtml: Read apple, lychee or mango. Load fruits.csv and retain rows with that label. Create X from size_cm and sweetness, and y from label in that same order. Print X_shape=(R, 2) and y_count=R on separate lines.
hints: Filter the complete frame once before creating either array.

practice.title: Calculate histogram boundaries honestly
practice.statementHtml: Read one or more integer sizes from 0 through 10. For intervals [0,5) and [5,10], print the bin counts as a Python list and then total=N. Include the final endpoint 10.
hints: Use np.histogram with edges [0,5,10] and sum its counts.

practice.title: Repair a column broadcast
practice.statementHtml: You have X of shape (5,2) and one offset per fruit in v of shape (5,). Write the corrected addition and explain the failed form.
hints: Create the missing singleton column dimension.
practice.answerHtml: Use X + v.reshape(5, 1) or X + v[:, None]. The failed form compares trailing lengths 2 and 5. The repaired (5,1) column compares 2 with 1, so each fruit’s offset covers its two entries. The result stays (5,2).

practice.title: Choose three plots
practice.statementHtml: Name a plot for fruit size versus sweetness, cumulative runs after each over, and fruit-weight frequency. State the meaning of one mark in each.
hints: Match paired measurements, sequence and distribution to different views.
practice.answerHtml: Scatter: one dot is a fruit’s paired size and sweetness. Line: a point is the cumulative total after an over and a segment connects successive totals. Histogram: one bar counts fruit weights in an interval. Add units and state bin endpoints.

practice.title: Discuss a selection bias
practice.statementHtml: A class measures only large display mangoes and uses that table to describe all fruit at the market. Explain the problem without blaming the pupils.
hints: Ask which fruits had a chance to enter the collection.
practice.answerHtml: The collection excludes small fruits and other labels, so it cannot describe the market’s full variety. The issue is the sampling plan, not the pupils’ arithmetic. Define the question, include the relevant kinds and sizes, and record how cards were selected. More copies of the same display mangoes would not repair the missing coverage.

practice.title: Keep exploration separate from decisions
practice.statementHtml: A study-time group has lower recorded marks. Why can a group mean not justify judging an individual pupil’s effort or future result?
hints: Consider absent measurements, unmeasured circumstances and invented data.
practice.answerHtml: A group mean hides variation and cannot explain an individual. Missing records, different learning opportunities and other measurements could affect it. Here the records and relationships are invented, so they are teaching material rather than evidence about pupils. Any real use would need a valid question, appropriate data, consent and accountable human review.

quiz.prompt: Warm-up A: what shape describes the measurement table in the picture?
quiz.explanation: There are five records and two feature columns. The picture is a row-by-feature table.

caption.en: Five records, two measurements in each record.

quiz.prompt: Warm-up B: which fruit label has the larger mean size in the summary picture?
options: apple, with mean 6.8 cm
mango, with mean 6.8 cm
mango, because it has more rows
Both means are 5 cm
quiz.explanation: Both groups have five rows. Compare their mean column: apples average 3.4 cm and mangoes 6.8 cm.

caption.en: Size summaries of all ten shared fruit cards.
caption.bn: শেয়ার করা দশটি ফলের আকারের সারাংশ।

quiz.prompt: Warm-up C: which claim about p6 is justified by the scatter picture?
options: Its label is definitely wrong
Every large fruit must be sour
It is far from the other mangoes in the plotted measurements and deserves inspection
Removing p6 must improve a future model
quiz.explanation: The isolated point suggests a question. Validity and the effect of removing it need additional evidence.

caption.en: Six invented fruits; the rightmost mango is unlike the other mangoes.
caption.bn: ছয়টি বানানো ফল; সবচেয়ে ডানের আমটি অন্য আমগুলোর চেয়ে আলাদা।

quiz.prompt: Code reading A: which matrix results from a row offset?
quiz.explanation: Add 1 to column zero and 10 to column one, preserving two rows and two columns.
quiz.code:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[2, 3], [6, 7]])
print((X + [1, 10]).tolist())

quiz.prompt: Code reading B: what shape preserves one feature as a table?
quiz.explanation: A slice retains its column dimension, giving three rows and one column.
quiz.code:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[2, 3], [6, 7], [7, 8]])
print(X[:, :1].shape)

quiz.prompt: Code reading C: which value is selected by position rather than by label?
quiz.explanation: Position one is the second row. Its size is 6 even though its label is 10.
quiz.code:
import pandas as pd
f = pd.DataFrame({"size": [2, 6, 7]}, index=[30, 10, 20])
print(f.iloc[1, 0])

quiz.prompt: Code reading D: what apple mean does groupby compute?
quiz.explanation: The apple group contains sizes 2 and 4, whose mean is 3.0. Mango size 8 belongs to another group.
quiz.code:
import pandas as pd
f = pd.DataFrame({"label": ["apple", "mango", "apple"], "size": [2, 8, 4]})
means = f.groupby("label")["size"].mean()
print(f"{means['apple']:.1f}")

quiz.prompt: Code reading E: which vector contains the feature totals?
quiz.explanation: axis=0 combines rows: sizes sum to 15 and sweetness values sum to 18.
quiz.code:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[2, 3], [6, 7], [7, 8]])
print(X.sum(axis=0).tolist())

quiz.prompt: A (5,2) matrix needs one independent offset per fruit. Which offset shape fits?
quiz.explanation: Trailing length one stretches across two feature columns, while the leading length five matches fruits.

quiz.prompt: Which operation keeps a table’s measurements together while ordering by size?
options: Sort only the label vector
Sort the complete DataFrame by size_cm
Sort every column independently
Reshape all values into a single row
quiz.explanation: A complete-row sort carries every feature and label together.

quiz.prompt: Which plot best answers how the distribution of fruit weights is spread?
options: A line through arbitrary fruit order
A scatter of row index against label codes
A histogram of weight_g
A legend without data
quiz.explanation: Histogram bins count the weights in ranges. Choose and label bin edges.

quiz.prompt: Which plot best shows the relation between size and sweetness?
options: A histogram of size only
A line joining unrelated CSV rows
A list of library versions
A scatter plot with one dot per fruit
quiz.explanation: Both measurements appear together at each dot; a one-variable histogram cannot show their pairing.

quiz.prompt: Why is final marks a poor input for predicting passed before an exam?
options: It reveals the outcome and is unavailable at the prediction time
It is always text
It has too few decimal places
Its column name is long
quiz.explanation: The target was constructed from final marks. Earlier availability matters when selecting features.

quiz.prompt: Which action improves access to a fruit-label plot for a reader who cannot distinguish its colours?
options: Remove the axis units
Use different marker shapes and a named legend too
Use colour as the only cue
Hide the caption
quiz.explanation: Redundant visual cues preserve label meaning when colour alone is insufficient.

quiz.prompt: Why does a numeric type check not catch every invalid observation?
options: Numeric arrays contain no values
CSV imports always delete errors
An impossible measurement can still be a valid numeric value
pandas never reports types
quiz.explanation: Thirty study hours per day parses as a number but conflicts with the unit and its physical limit.

quiz.prompt: What must match when applying a Boolean mask to X and y?
options: The labels must be alphabetically sorted alone
Both arrays must have two feature columns
Every mask entry must be True
The mask must refer to their same original row order
quiz.explanation: A shared mask preserves pairings only if the source arrays already describe matching rows.

quiz.prompt: Why record versions as well as a random seed?
options: Library behaviour and random streams can change between releases
Seeds erase software differences
Version strings predict fruit labels
Versions make all records representative
quiz.explanation: A seed controls a starting state within an implementation; environment records preserve implementation context.

quiz.prompt: A real school wants to use the invented study table to allocate scholarships. What is a responsible response?
options: Rank pupils from the example means
Do not use this teaching table as evidence for decisions about actual pupils
Treat missing study time as proof of low effort
Assume the invented relationships hold everywhere
quiz.explanation: The data are fictional and not collected for that decision. Representation, consent, validity and review would require a separate process.

keyPoints.bn: array-এর ফলের মান আর shape দুটোই মিলিয়ে দেখো।

keyPoints.bn: সারির label আর অবস্থানের ঠিকানা আলাদা করে বোঝো।

keyPoints.bn: ছবির প্রতিটি চিহ্ন কী বোঝায়, বলো।

keyPoints.bn: group-এর গড়ে সংশ্লিষ্ট উপস্থিত মানের সংখ্যা ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: Preserve paired records during selection and sorting.
keyPoints.bn: বাছাই আর সাজানোর সময় রেকর্ডের জোড়াগুলো ঠিক রাখো।

keyPoints.en: Fictional course data cannot justify real pupil decisions.
keyPoints.bn: কোর্সের বানানো data দিয়ে বাস্তব শিক্ষার্থীর সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া যায় না।

examQuestions.question: For X=[[2,3],[3,2],[4,3],[6,7],[7,8]], give shape, ndim, total size and column means.
examQuestions.answerHtml: shape=(5,2), ndim=2 and size=10. Column totals are [22,23]. Divide each by five: means [4.4,4.6]. size counts entries, whereas shape preserves their arrangement.

examQuestions.question: Add [10,20] to the five-row matrix above. Give all rows and the total.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The rows are [12,23], [13,22], [14,23], [16,27], [17,28]. Original total is 45. The offsets add 30 in each of five rows, adding 150; the new total is 195.

examQuestions.question: Add column offsets [1,2,3,4,5] to that same X after reshaping the offsets to (5,1).
examQuestions.answerHtml: The result is [[3,4],[5,4],[7,6],[10,11],[12,13]]. Each row receives its offset twice. The total increases by 2×(1+2+3+4+5)=30 from 45 to 75.

examQuestions.question: An ordered frame has row labels [10,20,30,40,50]. Give labels from loc[20:40] and iloc[1:3].
examQuestions.answerHtml: loc selects labels 20,30,40 including the endpoint. iloc selects positions one and two, corresponding to labels 20,30. Its stop position three is excluded.

examQuestions.question: Five apple sizes are [2,3,3,4,5]; five mango sizes are [6,7,8,7,6]. Compute grouped counts and means.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Both counts are five. Apples sum to 17 and average 3.4 cm. Mangoes sum to 34 and average 6.8 cm. The overall mean is 51/10=5.1 cm. The equal group sizes make the mean of these two means equal the overall mean in this case.

examQuestions.question: A six-row Series is [2,3,missing,4,missing,7]. Give row count, present count, missing count and mean.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Rows=6, present=4, missing=2. Present values sum to 16, yielding mean 4.0. Filling missing cells with zero would yield 16/6 instead and assert something absent from the original records.

examQuestions.question: For histogram data [2,3,4,6,7,9] and edges [0,3,6,9], explain all endpoint decisions.
examQuestions.answerHtml: 2 goes in [0,3); 3 and 4 go in [3,6); 6,7,9 go in final [6,9]. Counts [1,2,3] sum to six. Interior endpoints go to the bin on their right; the final endpoint is included.

examQuestions.question: Plan an offline fruit exploration script that a classmate can reproduce.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Preserve the course CSV, Python source and library versions. Read the header, inspect missingness, count labels and record the feature order. Use seeded generators if randomness is added. Save a labelled scatter figure with Agg and close it. Run the script from a fresh process with the CSV in the working directory.

examQuestions.question: Distinguish entrywise multiplication and a dot product for [6,7] and [2,1].
examQuestions.answerHtml: Entrywise multiplication gives [12,7]; the dot product adds those entries and gives 19. NumPy spells them with * and @ respectively for these vectors. One keeps two values, while the other combines the features into one scalar.

examQuestions.question: A classroom table is proposed for deciding real scholarships. Explain the review needed before any such use.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The course table is invented and should not make real allocation decisions. For a separate real project, establish purpose, consent, measurement validity and representative coverage. Check missingness, available-at-decision-time features and unequal error costs. Provide human review and an appeal route. Descriptive group means alone cannot justify individual judgements.
